correctness.rationale: Every factor with at least two ones contains a unique zero gap, fixing its only possible location. Exact zero-run left/right margins prove the two candidate minimal obstructions and exclude all others; a separate triple-one edge argument rules out any minimal absence with three ones. The two families give the rational length series, nonregularity via a regular intersection, and a deterministic pushdown recognition construction. The first occurrence of \(0^N\) proves the sharp prefix lower bound, while explicit earliest-occurrence bounds cover all other N-factors. Standard-library exhaustive verification succeeds for all lengths 1 through 26, including minimal-absence sets and sharp cutoffs. Enumeration is explicitly finite, not the basis of the universal proof.

value.rationale: The antidictionary is a standard intrinsic invariant of infinite words and string indexing. This proves an all-length natural language classification for the basic strictly-increasing-gap triangular-marker word, gives its exact length profile and nonregular deterministic context-free status, and establishes the sharp finite prefix needed for all factors and MAWs to any cutoff. The claim is not an arbitrary numerical slice, renaming, finite experiment or the already-known factor-complexity count. Scope is explicitly limited to this specific word.
